intended_object: For a group G acting on X and a fixed point x (g • x = x for every g in G), the canonical group isomorphism between the isotropy (automorphism) group of x in the action groupoid G ⋉ X and G. Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation: The body composes three isomorphisms: the inverse of the library's Aut(x) ≃* stabilizer isomorphism, the identification of the stabilizer with the whole group (Subgroup.eq_top_iff' applied to the fixed-point hypothesis), and Subgroup.topEquiv. The result sends an automorphism to its label, as the simp lemma autMulEquivOfMemFixedPoints_apply shows. The multiplication conventions agree: Aut composes as g * h = h ≫ g, which matches the stabilizer, so this is a genuine group isomorphism and not an anti-isomorphism. The setting, a group acting on an arbitrary type, is the standard one for the action groupoid. Mathlib has stabilizerIsoEnd, which relates the stabilizer to the endomorphism monoid at x, but I found no Mathlib declaration identifying Aut(x) with G at a fixed point.
